div.head: Leis Wl 47
div.ab: E cil qui est redté e testimoniet de deleauté, e le plait tres foiz eschuit, e al quart mustrent li sumenour de se[s] treis defautes, uncore le mande l’um, que il plege truse e vienge a dreit.

De rectato qui uocatus non comparet. Si quis malam habens famam et de infidelitate rectatus tercio uocatus non comparet, quarto die ostendant summonitores tres defaltas, et adhuc summonicionem habeat, ut plegios inueniat et iuri pareat.
E cil qui est redté e testimoniet de deleauté e le plait tres foiz eschuit, e al quart mustrent li sumenour de se[s] treis defautes, uncore le mande l'um que il plege truse e vienge a dreit.

47. Und wer [= wenn einer] bescholten und durch Zeugniss wegen Unredlichkeit beleumundet ist und die Gerichtsverhandlung dreimal vermeidet, und [wenn] beim vierten [Gericht] die Vorlader seine drei [Termin-]Versäumnisse darlegen, fordere man ihn nochmals auf, dass er Bürgschaft finde und zu Recht erscheine.

47. And whoever [= if one] is ill-reputed and accused by testimony of dishonesty and avoids the court proceedings three times, and [if] at the fourth [court] the summoners set forth his three defaults [of term], one shall summon him once more to find surety and appear to stand to law.

And if anyone who is accused and against whom evidence of untrustworthiness is given fails three times to attend the court proceedings, and if, at the fourth meeting of the court, the summoners bring forward his three defections, he shall once more be asked to find a surety and appear before the court.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 272–273 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 518, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: Ebd. Vorladung 7a. Für gerichtlich hält die Vorlader Moisy Gloss. Anglo-Normand 934, mit Zitat aus Britton [Ende 13. Jhs.!]: Les sominours soient chargés de estre illonques mesme le jour à tesmoyner lour sumounse. Dies bezweifelt Opet Prozesseinleitung 56. Auch besoldete Vorlader zum Reichsrat heissen aber 1164 ebenso; Stubbs Constit. hist. I 467{3}

Ibid. Vorladung 7a. Moisy (Gloss. Anglo-Normand 934) takes the summoners to be officers of the court, quoting Britton [end of the 13th cent.!]: Les sominours soient chargés de estre illonques mesme le jour à tesmoyner lour sumounse. Opet (Prozesseinleitung 56) doubts this. But salaried summoners to the king’s council are also so called in 1164; Stubbs Constit. hist. I 467{3}
